generic_line: Provider not detected. Allow inbound TCP 80 and 443 (keep 22 for SSH) in your provider's firewall or security group.
provider_line:
Provider: {name} (detected from {source})
Create these inbound rules:
flag_json: print the rules as JSON to stdout and nothing else
usage:
Usage:
  {prog} doctor cloud [--json]
  {prog} doctor --cloud [--json]

Prints the inbound firewall rules (names, ports 80 and 443) and the console
link for the cloud provider this server runs on, from its metadata service.
An unknown provider gets the generic ports line.

Flags:
explain_usage:
Usage:
  {prog} {label} <check-id> [flags]

Explains one doctor check in plain words: what is wrong, why it matters and the
next step. The check id is the check_id field of the doctor report. The text is a
fixed table, no network lookup is involved.

Flags:
{flags}
reach_usage:
Usage:
  {prog} {label} [flags]

Which ports this server listens on, and whether the internet can reach them.
The outside check is off until the runtime setting doctor.reachability_dialback_url is set;
enabling it sends the port list to that URL, which learns this server's public IP.

Flags:
{flags}
paths_flag_json: print the paths as JSON to stdout and nothing else
paths_usage:
Usage:
  {prog} doctor paths [flags]

Prints where the binary, releases dir, data dir and systemd unit live on this host.
It never contacts a control plane.

Flags:
domains_doctor_flag_json: print the doctor report as JSON to stdout and nothing else
domains_doctor_usage:
Usage:
  {prog} domains doctor <app> <domain> [flags]

Runs every domain check (DNS per resolver, CAA, ports 80 and 443, TLS
certificate, HTTP status, redirects, HSTS, proxy ownership, app state,
certificate renewal) and prints a prioritised fix list. It only connects to
<domain> when the domain resolves to this server; otherwise it runs the DNS
checks and says why.

Flags:
  --token string          API token (default: {token_env} env var, then the credentials file)
  --api-url string       control plane base URL (default: {api_env} env var, then {api_url})
  --profile string       named credentials profile to read (overrides APP_PROFILE, default "default")
  --json                    print the report as JSON to stdout, nothing else
  --output string          output format: json, table, or text (default table; --json is shorthand for --output json)
  --query string           JMESPath expression to filter the result before printing
  -h, --help               show this help
domains_summary_flag_json: print the summary as JSON to stdout and nothing else
domains_summary_usage:
Usage:
  {prog} domains summary [--json]

Counts domains by status, certificates expiring or failing, and the total needing attention.
domains_summary_domains_line: {total} (live {live}, propagating {propagating}, waiting for DNS {waiting}, not set up {not_set_up}, paused {paused}, unknown {unknown})
domains_summary_certs_line: {expiring} expiring within {days} days, {expired} expired, {failing} failing to renew
domains_activity_flag_json: print the activity page as JSON to stdout and nothing else
domains_activity_usage:
Usage:
  {prog} domains activity <domain> [--limit N] [--before CURSOR] [--actions PREFIXES] [--json]

Lists a domain's recent changes and certificate events, newest first.
